newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh raises urea fertiliser price by 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh raises urea fertiliser price by 30 pct.

text.p: Bangladesh has raised the price of urea fertiliser by nearly 30 percent to cut subsidies and check smuggling, government officials said on Tuesday.
The cabinet, at a meeting late on Monday, approved a new price of 240 taka per 50-kg bag from a previous 186 taka.
The officials said the cabinet rejected an Industry Ministry proposal to raise the price to 275 taka per bag.

A senior official of the Industry Ministry, which controls the production and import of urea, said prices would still be far below international levels and the subsidy would remain at least 700 taka per tonne, costing the exchequer about four billion taka in 1997/98 (July-June).
He said the subsidy might rise to five billion taka as the government was planning to import a composite fertiliser, diammonium phosphate, for subsidised distribution among farmers.
The government has targeted production of two million tonnes of urea fertiliser and imports of another 0.5 million tonnes in 1997/98.
The subsidy was expected to reach 4.25 billion taka in 1996/97, ending June 30, when state-owned fertiliser factories were forecast to produce 2.2 million tonnes.
The ministry imported another 0.3 million tonnes in the current fiscal year to meet a shortfall and for emergency stocks.

Officials said the increase had also been decided upon to match the price in India, where a 50-kg bag sells at 226 rupees (equivalent to 240 taka). They said India had increased its price by 10 percent recently.
"The rise became inevitable to check smuggling (to India) although the high level of subsidy was also a big concern," one official said.
The variation with heavily subsidised Bangladesh prices often causes large-scale smuggling to India and Burma.
